Keys — R restart · Space play/pause · H hide this panel · F frame meter · Shot blur corrects a real optical fact: at a fixed framing, blur relative to the frame depends only on aperture diameter (focal length ÷ f-stop) — sensor size cancels — so the portrait shot's shallower look cannot be recomposed away in Blender. The gain is derived so each shot ENDS its rack at the same blur as the wide shot (portrait lands on ×2.69); the slider retunes whichever shot is on screen. Shot — the viewer carries two composed cameras and picks by viewport aspect (portrait below 1:1), re-picking on rotate; ?cam=cam_wide|cam_portrait pins one. P toggles a 30 Hz cadence lock (it ships free-running at 60; the lock only helps a machine that cannot hold 60). Rack start / land — the focus pull is authored in blur space: the subject is 100 m from a lens focused at 0.25–86 m, so the whole ring is a uniform blur whose radius goes as 1/focus-distance; Blender's distance-eased curve therefore pins the blur at maximum and then resolves in under half a second. The viewer instead runs the radius along a perceptually even (log-radius) sine S-curve between the two times; ?rack=blender restores the authored track. Framing / band are preview-only tools for recomposing the end pose in Blender: framing tightens the field of view and reads out the equivalent — ×1.5 = a 75 mm lens on the same camera position, or dollying in to 2/3 of the distance; band letterboxes the canvas to a hero-band shape (a 50%-height landing-page band is ~3.3:1 on a laptop, ~0.93:1 on a phone). The viewer is vertical-fit, so compose for the ring's share of the frame height; the sides breathe with the band's width. Nothing here ships — dial the look, take the number to Blender, rebake.

v2 scene: Cycles + AgX, seven lights — three glTF points plus four area lights rebuilt as RectAreaLights from a sidecar (glTF cannot carry them; intensities are Blender-native P/πA, driven per frame from the authored energy ramps). The world is the authored HDRI-through-luma-ramp, baked offline to an equirect that serves as background and IBL. Ring textures are pre-baked from the authored Mix/ColorRamp math into canonical glTF images (nothing dropped). Exposure 1.00 / contrast 0 calibrated against Cycles reference renders (within ~10%%). Shadows ship OFF: the area rig cannot cast in three, and the point fills cost 18 cube-map passes for a 2%% shift on chrome. The logo is a plate under the dome, read by the final top-down camera; its alphaCutoff is 0.12 because a 0.5 cutoff erodes thin glyphs at minified mips. Depth of field uses the real lens (50 mm f/10).
